assumptions.context: Sprint 3 brief calls for keeping dicer's 'error' listener live through cleanup so late-tick errors are routed through logger instead of escaping as uncaughtException. The discriminator can be implemented as either (a) two listeners (one swapped out at cleanup) or (b) a single listener that branches on a `cleaned` flag
assumptions.choice: Single listener with a `cleaned` flag branch. The handler reads `if (cleaned) { logger.warn ... } else { queue.signalError(err) }`. The flag is set as the FIRST mutation inside cleanup() so the discriminator is sequence-consistent — once cleanup begins, every subsequent dicer 'error' goes through the logger path. This shape minimizes listener-attach/detach churn and matches the architecture.md §4.4 description ('the lingering error listener fires; library calls logger.warn')
alternatives_considered: Two-listener-swap: attach a 'pre-cleanup' listener at construction, remove it in cleanup, attach a 'post-cleanup' listener at the end of cleanup (rejected — leaves a tick window where dicer 'error' could fire with no listener attached and crash the process; the brief explicitly says 'KEEP dicer's error listener attached')

assumptions.context: FR-022 truncation detection: when source emits 'end' but dicer hasn't emitted 'finish'. Naively pushing MultipartTruncatedError on source 'end' (synchronous from the listener) race-trips well-formed envelopes — Readable.from(buf) emits 'end' BEFORE dicer's pipe-driven 'finish' lands on a subsequent process.nextTick.
assumptions.choice: Defer the dicerFinished check to setImmediate inside onSourceEnd. setImmediate runs strictly AFTER any pending I/O and any already-scheduled process.nextTick / promise microtasks. Tested empirically: with this delay, well-formed envelopes pass dicerFinished===true at check time; truncated envelopes leave dicerFinished===false. Also added an `if (cleaned) return` short-circuit so a cleanup-then-source-end race doesn't push into a closed queue
alternatives_considered: Use process.nextTick instead of setImmediate (rejected — dicer's own end-of-stream emit uses process.nextTick chains, so a single nextTick doesn't necessarily run AFTER dicer's 'finish'; setImmediate is the next-macrotask boundary and reliably runs after)
Check dicerFinished synchronously and use a 'finish-pending' flag (rejected — adds a second flag and three race cases; the setImmediate approach is one flag and one race case)

assumptions.context: dicer's per-part Readables can emit 'error' (e.g. 'Part terminated early due to unexpected end of multipart data') when the source is destroyed mid-part. With NO listener attached, Node treats this as an unhandled 'error' event and crashes the process — the truncation tests T-066 / T-068 originally crashed the test worker because of this
assumptions.choice: Attach a per-part 'error' listener inside `onPart` immediately when dicer emits the part stream. Pre-cleanup the listener calls queue.signalError(err); post-cleanup it routes through logger.warn with the 'multipart: late part-stream error after generator close' message. This mirrors the dicer-level 'error' listener shape — same `cleaned` discriminator, same summarizeError meta
alternatives_considered: Set a global process.on('uncaughtException') in tests (rejected — masks real bugs and isn't a production fix)
Wait for the consumer to drain the part body before destroying it (rejected — break paths can't reach this; the unyielded parts are exactly what we need to clean up)
Drain dicer pre-destroy (rejected — adds wallclock to break and doesn't compose with truncation paths)

assumptions.context: queue.drainPendingParts() returns parts that the queue knows about (i.e. ones that reached `onHeader` and got pushed). But in synchronous source-error paths, the part may have been emitted on dicer's 'part' event WITHOUT yet reaching onHeader (so it never made it into the queue). T-068 originally failed because such a part stream was captured by the harness but not destroyed
assumptions.choice: Maintain an `allPartStreams = new Set<DicerPartStream>()` belt-and-suspenders set. Add to it inside onPart at construction time (synchronous from the dicer 'part' emit). On cleanup, after queue.drainPendingParts() destroys the queued parts, iterate allPartStreams and destroy any not-yet-destroyed entry. Then clear the set
alternatives_considered: Push to the queue earlier (rejected — would queue a half-formed StreamingMultipartPart with empty headers; the consumer's `for await` would yield a broken object)
Wait for onHeader before declaring the part 'tracked' (rejected — synchronous source-error paths terminate before onHeader fires)
